name: Regional Saturation
description: Primary region is saturated under concert ticket drop load. Failover to secondary is tempting but secondary has limited headroom — a full shift would cascade the problem.

commonAnnotations.summary: Primary region us-east-1 saturated at 89% capacity — checkout latency rising, secondary region has only 15% headroom.

logs: us-east-1 checkout pods at 89% CPU — approaching saturation
us-west-2 running at 85% capacity — only 15% headroom remaining
queue wait times increasing — users abandoning at 22% rate
payment latency stable but checkout throughput declining
traces: checkout spans show queuing delay 800ms+ in us-east-1
cross-region latency us-east-1 -> us-west-2 adds 45ms overhead
payment service healthy in both regions — not a dependency issue

candidate_actions.description: Shift traffic to the secondary region

restart_payment.notes: Payment is not the bottleneck — restarting it wastes time and changes nothing. The region remains saturated. Queue abandonment continues to climb.

disable_flag.notes: Disabling payment kills ticket purchasing during the concert drop. CPU drops because no one can buy anything. The incident is 'resolved' by destroying the business event.

rate_limit_retries.notes: Rate limiting reduces retry noise slightly, but the primary bottleneck is raw regional CPU saturation, not retry amplification. Latency improves marginally.

shift_traffic.notes: A cautious partial traffic shift moves 15-20% of checkout load to us-west-2, staying within its headroom. Primary region drops from 89% to ~72% CPU. Latency normalizes. Both regions remain healthy.

ground_truth.why: A cautious partial traffic shift redistributes load within secondary region headroom, relieving primary saturation without overwhelming the secondary. Both regions stay healthy and ticket purchasing continues.

naive_reflex.why: A tired engineer sees high latency and restarts payment, but payment is healthy — the bottleneck is regional CPU saturation. The restart wastes critical minutes while queue abandonment climbs.

evaluation_labels.reflex_rejected_reason: Restarting payment pods is a no-op — payment is healthy in both regions. The real bottleneck is regional CPU saturation from the concert traffic surge. Every minute spent on a pointless restart is a minute of 22%+ queue abandonment and lost ticket sales.
evaluation_labels.fairness_impact: Partial traffic shifting preserves fair access for all customers. Without it, users routed to the saturated primary region experience degraded checkout while secondary-region users are unaffected — creating an unfair split during a time-sensitive drop.
